failures.message: ran and passed with its mutant applied to saffron/task.py — With one `depends_on` entry, `run_task` returns `Refused` before any cell starts when the parent's chosen row is `REBUTTAL_UNJUDGED` and no push followed that state. The reason names the parent, `REBUTTAL_UNJUDGED` and that its latest run pushed nothing, and it never says a push was refused, since a crash or an older row refused nothing. No `unstacked` line prints, and no queue row is written. The witness drives three rows through `cli._run_cell` with a `gh` and through `cli._batch_runner` with none. They are no push, a stale push whose branch still points at it, and no push on a row newer than a pushed `READY_FOR_REVIEW` row. `run_batch` over that runner ends `DRAINED` and attaches no run. A stale push whose branch a review fix moved is refused too, in both `gh` modes. A push made in the state still stacks on the fetched head, as does a resumed row pushed again, on a branch a review fix moved past the recorded push. A row carrying a pull request is refused when a `gh` answers open and when it cannot answer. When it answers merged, the row refuses nothing. In both `gh` modes `READY_FOR_REVIEW`, `APPROVED`, `MERGE_TRAIN` and `REVIEW_INCOMPLETE` keep their old result, with a stale push and with none. With a `gh`, so does a stale `CHANGES_REQUESTED` row. A parent with a `MERGED` row, one retired at `base_sha`, and one with a push in `base_sha` each refuse nothing, in both `gh` modes. A retired parent with a stale push keeps its path and stacks on its branch. A row a reconcile moves to `MERGED` counts, so the rule reads the rows after it.

ran and passed with its mutant applied to saffron/task.py — With two or more `depends_on` entries, `_resolve_multi_parent` reads every open parent's chosen row before it picks the deepest. A parent refuses as in the one-parent rule, whatever its place. The witness drives the deepest parent, a shallower one on its chain, a parent off that chain, and two at once, each with no push and with a stale push, in both `gh` modes. The reason names each refused parent and no other, and an off-chain parent's reason names its latest run rather than the chain. Two parents pushed in the state, or resumed and pushed again, still stack on the deepest head. A parent with a `MERGED` row, one retired at `base_sha` and one with a push in `base_sha` are not open, so each carries a refused row and refuses nothing. A deepest `REVIEW_INCOMPLETE` parent with no push still starts unstacked. `run_task` returns `Refused` with no cell on one case through `cli._run_cell` with a `gh`, and one through `cli._batch_runner` with none.

payload.summary: 2 of 3 witness(es) survived their own mutant
